validity.recommendation: Escalate for primary-source check against SNGPL's actual transmission-line asset schedule (annual report technical annex or OGRA State of the (Regulated) Petroleum Industry report annex) before staging any refs. Specifically resolve the geometric contradiction between the stated 90.82 km length and the ~126.6 km straight-line distance between its own Faisalabad/Malakwal endpoints -- the Length value, the endpoint pairing, or the row's independent existence (vs. being a mislabeled fragment of P4128) is very likely wrong even if SNGPL does operate a real asset behind this row.
validity.researcher_notes:
gem.wiki returned HTTP 403 to the harvester for this whole scope, so wiki_citations.json has no cited source to start from for this row (confirmed empty entry: {'ok': false, 'status': 403}). This is therefore new research from a cold start, not a re-check of an existing citation.

Extensive open-web search (Bing, attempted Google/DuckDuckGo -- both blocked by CAPTCHA/error pages) across many phrasings -- exact phrase "Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline", "Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline II", "Malakwal" + "SNGPL", "Malakwal" + "gas pipeline" + "Mandi Bahauddin", OGRA/SNGPL annexure searches for a transmission-line table -- returned ZERO results referencing this pipeline, any gas-transmission asset serving Malakwal town, or this name anywhere online. Every query either returned generic Faisalabad tourism/geography pages, SNGPL bill-payment portals, or entirely unrelated content (one query returned University of Guelph library pages). SNGPL's public transmission-system page (sngpl.com.pk/web/about-us/transmission-system/) 404'd, so the utility's own site did not yield a network map either. Web Archive (web.archive.org) is not reachable from this environment, so I could not check an archived snapshot of the gem.wiki page for citation leads.

Independently verified the two endpoints' coordinates via Wikipedia (a source unrelated to GEM, used only for geography, not cited as a pipeline source): Faisalabad 31.4167N 73.0911E; Malakwal (Mandi Bahauddin District, Punjab) 32.5531N 73.2067E. Straight-line (great-circle) distance between those points is ~126.6 km. This row's own LengthKnown value is 90.82 km -- LESS than the straight-line distance between its own stated StartLocation/EndLocation. A pipeline route can never be shorter than the straight-line distance between its endpoints, so this is a self-contained, verifiable data error independent of any external source: either the Length, or one/both endpoint names, is wrong, or this row is not really a Faisalabad-to-Malakwal line at all (e.g. a mislabeled sub-segment of a longer corridor). For comparison, sibling row P4128 'Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline' (no numeral) states 158.67 km, which comfortably clears the 126.6 km floor and is a physically plausible route.

Roster context: the wider 63-row roster contains several other same-corridor 'Pipeline' / 'Pipeline II' pairs with internally consistent-looking specs (P4106/P4107 Sidhnai-Faisalabad, P4135/P4136 Faisalabad-Shahdara I/II, P4161/P4162 Dandot-Gali Jagir-Wah I/II, P4170/P4173 Wah-Nowshera I/II, P4108/P4140 Sahiwal-Lahore I/II), which argues the underlying table is probably a genuine SNGPL segment inventory rather than wholesale fabrication -- but that context does not rescue this specific row's internal length/endpoint contradiction, and I could not find one independent trace of THIS row anywhere to confirm it as a distinct, correctly-specified asset. Owner (SNGPL, 100%) is geographically plausible (SNGPL is the correct Punjab transmission operator) but likewise unconfirmed by any independent source.

No refs are proposed for Status, Fuel, PipelineType, Diameter, Location, or Owner on this row -- none could be independently verified, and per standing rules I will not fabricate a URL or force a citation onto an unverifiable value.

summary: P4129 (Faisalabad-Malakwal Gas Pipeline II): existence concern -- zero independent corroboration found after extensive multi-engine search, plus the stated 90.82 km length is geometrically impossible for its own named endpoints (~126.6 km straight-line apart, per independently verified coordinates); all 7 MISSING_REF units (Status/Fuel/PipelineType/Length/Diameter/Location/Owner) left UNRESOLVED, no refs staged.
